name: TV DIABLO Windows
note: v3339: The second-eye ledger stores the HEAD of each answer so a plausible summary cannot stand in for a look, and judging whether a stored verdict still means what it says requires knowing whether the whole answer is there. THE CAP WAS WRITTEN IN FOUR PLACES: three slices in the runner, 200 on each unreached path and 400 on the reached one, plus the writer own constant of 600. The runner cut FIRST, so a row capped at 400 never reached 600 and the re-judger treated it as a whole answer. MEASURED on 843 rows: 381 sat at exactly 400 while prefixOnly reported 98, and the census, counting only the writer 600, reported 91. Two readings disagreeing because one number lived in four places. Now the runner passes the FULL answer and DECLARES its cap, the writer cuts ONCE and records headCap on the row, and the re-judger asks the row rather than a constant. RE-MEASURED on 847 rows: prefixOnly 478 and agree fell from 554 to 192. THREE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-TWO ROWS LEFT AGREEMENT FOR UNKNOWN, which is the only honest direction, because the ledger had been claiming agreement it could not support. ⚠ A legacy row carries no headCap and nothing on disk says which cap applied, so 200, 400 and 600 are all treated as prefix-only: that can only REMOVE claimed agreement and never manufacture it. ⚠ The default resolves at CALL time rather than in the signature, because the constant is defined BELOW the writer in that file and a signature default would not even import. 3 red-proofs PROVEN, 469 gates. ⚠ MY OWN EDIT LANDED IN THE WRONG FUNCTION FIRST: the cap line was inserted into agreement rather than record, where the name it reads does not exist, and only running the function found it. A find that lands on the next matching shape is not the shape you meant.
